2027-04-01.title: Thursday within the Octave of Easter
readings: You killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead. To this we are witnesses
O Lord, our God, how wonderful your name in all the earth! (or: Alleluia)
Thus it is written, that the Messiah is to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day
2027-04-01.alt: Day within the Octave of Easter, kept with the rank of a solemnity. The Gloria is sung; the Easter Sequence may be sung before the Gospel acclamation; the dismissal has the double Alleluia. Liturgical colour: white. Today is also the first Thursday of the month, kept in many parishes with prayer for priests and for vocations. Seventh day of the Divine Mercy Novena.
2027-04-01.verse: Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself. Touch me and see; for a ghost does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.
theo: The lame man who was healed at the Beautiful Gate will not let go of Peter and John. He clings to them, and the whole crowd comes running to Solomon's Portico, “utterly astonished.” Peter sees the faces turned towards him and refuses the glory at once: “why do you stare at us, as though by our own power or piety we had made him walk?” The power is not theirs. “The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of our ancestors has glorified his servant Jesus.” Then Peter tells the story of Good Friday in a few sharp words: the Holy and Righteous One was rejected, a murderer was preferred, “and you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead. To this we are witnesses.” What a title for the crucified Lord: the Author of life, the one from whom all life begins, put to death, and death could not hold him.

Peter does not speak as an accuser who wants to crush his hearers. He is himself a man who denied the Lord three times only a few weeks before. So his next words are full of tenderness: “And now, friends, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did also your rulers.” They echo the prayer of Jesus on the cross: Father, forgive them. The Church has always refused to lay the death of Christ on the Jewish people as a whole; the Second Vatican Council taught this plainly (Nostra Aetate 4), and the Catechism adds that all sinners were the authors of his Passion, we Christians most of all (CCC 597–598). Peter's call is to everyone, then and now: “Repent therefore, and turn to God so that your sins may be wiped out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord.” He reminds them that they are heirs of the promise made to Abraham: “in your descendants all the families of the earth shall be blessed.” The Risen One was sent “first to you, to bless you.” The Psalm marvels at the dignity God gives to frail human beings: “what are human beings that you are mindful of them, mortals that you care for them?” The Letter to the Hebrews reads this psalm of Jesus, crowned with glory after the suffering of death.

In the Gospel the two disciples from Emmaus are still telling their story when Jesus himself stands among them and says, “Peace be with you.” Instead of joy there is terror: “They were startled and terrified, and thought that they were seeing a ghost.” The Lord answers their fear with his body: “Why are you frightened, and why do doubts arise in your hearts? Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself. Touch me and see; for a ghost does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.” Luke adds one of the most human lines in the Gospels: “in their joy they were disbelieving and still wondering.” The news is too good to believe. So Jesus asks, “Have you anything here to eat?” They give him a piece of broiled fish, and he eats it in their presence. The Risen Lord is not a memory, not a vision, not a spirit floating above the earth. He is the same Jesus, with the same body that was nailed to the cross, now raised to a glory that will never die.

Then he does what he did on the road to Emmaus: “he opened their minds to understand the scriptures.” Everything written about him “in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms” had to be fulfilled: the Messiah was to suffer and to rise on the third day, “and that repentance and forgiveness of sins is to be proclaimed in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. You are witnesses of these things.” Notice how today's two readings answer each other. In the Gospel Jesus says, “You are witnesses”; in Acts Peter stands in the Temple and says, “To this we are witnesses.” The Church is born as a community of witnesses to a real, bodily Resurrection. The Collect of the day prays for the newly baptized, that the many nations united in confessing his name may be one in faith and in deeds. That is the Easter mission: to carry repentance and forgiveness to every nation, beginning from our own Jerusalem, our home and our parish.
conn: A covered colonnade on the east side of the Temple courts. Jesus walked there at the feast of Dedication (John 10:23), and the first Christians often gathered there (Acts 5:12).

The Greek word archēgos means leader, founder, pioneer: the one who goes first and opens the way. Hebrews 2:10 calls Jesus the “pioneer of their salvation.” The one who gives life could not be held by death.

Peter echoes Luke 23:34, “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.” The Catechism quotes this verse (CCC 597) in teaching that the Jews are not collectively responsible for the death of Jesus.
Peter looks forward to the return of Christ in glory, when God will make all things new (Acts 3:20–21; Revelation 21:5).
Moses' promise in Deuteronomy 18:15–19. The early Church saw Jesus as the new Moses, the prophet to whom all must listen.

The Risen Lord eats not because he needs food but to show that he is truly alive in his body. Peter will later preach that the witnesses “ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead” (Acts 10:41).
The Law, the Prophets and the Psalms.
The three parts of the Hebrew Scriptures as they were known in Jesus' day; the Psalms head the third part, the Writings. Jesus says all of them speak of him.
Hebrews 2:6–9 reads this psalm of Christ: made for a little while lower than the angels, “now crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death.”
altar: The Lord who ate the broiled fish before his disciples now gives himself to us as food. The Body we receive at Mass is not a symbol of a departed teacher but the living, risen body of Christ, glorious and real, which once bore the nails.

Before Communion the priest says, “The peace of the Lord be with you always.” It is the Easter greeting of the Risen One standing among his frightened friends. Receive it as he gave it: as peace that drives out fear.
outline: Ask: have you ever received news so good you could not believe it?
Point 1 · Not by our own power
The healed man and Peter's humility.
Repentance and forgiveness to all nations.
A piece of broiled fish on a table, and wounded hands taking it.
“Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself.”
live: When someone praises you today for a good deed, quietly turn it to God, as Peter did: it was not by my own power.
Ask the Risen Lord tonight to open your mind to the Scriptures, and read Luke 24:36–48 slowly.
Tell one person in your family how the Lord has helped you this Lent or this Easter.
On this first Thursday, pray for the priest who baptized you and for the priests of your parish.
fathers: St Ignatius of Antioch (Letter to the Smyrnaeans 3, in substance)

I know and believe that he was in the flesh even after the resurrection. When he came to Peter and those with him, he said: take hold of me, handle me and see that I am not a bodiless ghost. And they touched him and believed. After his resurrection he ate and drank with them as one who was in the flesh.

The Lord ate after his resurrection not because he was hungry but because he was able. The earth soaks up water in one way; the sun draws it up in another. He took food by power, not by need, so that his disciples might be sure his body was real.
St Leo the Great (Sermon on the Ascension, in substance)

Those days between the Resurrection and the Ascension were not spent idly. In them the Lord let himself be touched, ate with his disciples and opened the Scriptures, so that every doubt might be healed and our faith built on firm ground.
magis: The risen Jesus invites his disciples to touch him and shares their meal; his body is real, yet now possesses new properties of a glorious body.
The Jews are not collectively responsible for Jesus' death; all sinners were the authors of his Passion.
What happened in the Passion cannot be charged against all the Jews then living, nor against the Jews of today.
How do the dead rise? Christ is raised with his own body; we too shall rise with our own bodies.
The New Testament lies hidden in the Old, and the Old is made manifest in the New.
saints: Bishop of Grenoble (died 1132), commemorated in the Roman Martyrology on 1 April. He welcomed St Bruno and his six companions and gave them the wild valley of the Chartreuse, where the Carthusian Order began in 1084. His day is not kept this year because of the Octave.

2 Apr: Friday within the Octave (no abstinence). 3 Apr: Saturday within the Octave. 4 Apr: Second Sunday of Easter, Sunday of Divine Mercy. 5 Apr: the Annunciation of the Lord (transferred from 25 March).
2027-04-01.prayer: O God, who have united the many nations in confessing your name, grant that those reborn in the font of Baptism may be one in the faith of their hearts and the homage of their deeds. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Risen Lord Jesus, you stood among your frightened disciples and said, Peace be with you. Show us your hands and your feet when we doubt, open our minds to understand the Scriptures, and send us out as witnesses of repentance and forgiveness, beginning in our own homes. Alleluia. Amen.

quick: Peter: not by our power, but the God of our ancestors has glorified his servant Jesus, the Author of life.
Jesus shows his hands and feet and eats broiled fish: his Resurrection is real and bodily.
He opens the Scriptures and sends his disciples as witnesses of forgiveness to all nations.
2027-04-01.action: Pray tonight with your family for the priests of your parish, and thank God for one sign of his help this week.
2027-04-01.question: When good news from God seems too good to be true, do I let my joy turn into disbelief, or into praise?
catechism: The risen body of Jesus, real and glorious.
The Jews are not collectively responsible for Jesus' death.
Conversion: turning to God and away from sin, as Peter preached.
kidsaint: A story tells that Bishop Hugh once dreamed that God was building a house in the mountains and seven stars were leading the way. Soon seven men came to him, led by St Bruno, asking for a quiet place to pray. Hugh gave them a valley in the mountains, and the Carthusian monks still pray there today. Lesson: when God sends people to us, we can help them do his work.
2027-04-01.special: Thursday within the Octave of Easter (solemnity): Gloria; the Easter Sequence may be sung; double Alleluia at the dismissal. First Thursday of the month.
term: In Greek martys, the word from which “martyr” comes. A witness tells what he has seen and heard, and stakes his life on it. The Apostles were witnesses of the Resurrection, and most of them gave their lives for it.

family.explain: The friends of Jesus were talking together when suddenly Jesus was there with them! They were frightened and thought he was a ghost. Jesus said: look at my hands and my feet, touch me. Then he asked for something to eat, and they gave him a piece of fish. Jesus was really alive, with a real body.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who is afraid, that Jesus may give them his peace.
family.ask: Ask: “What would you say to Jesus if he came into our home tonight?” Then greet one another with: Peace be with you.

illus: A young fisherman from Poovar was lost at sea for four days after a storm. His family had already lit lamps for him and the parish had prayed for the dead. On the fifth morning he walked up the beach, thin and burnt by the sun. His old mother would not come near him; she kept saying, it is his spirit. He laughed, sat down on the steps and said, Amma, give me some kanji, I am starving. Only when she saw him eat did she run and hold him. The Risen Lord did the same for his frightened friends: he ate, so that they would believe.

pm.open: Risen Lord Jesus, stand among us now and say to us, Peace be with you. Open our minds to understand your word. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Not by our own power (Acts 3:12). Where am I tempted to take the glory that belongs to God?
Touch me and see (Luke 24:39). How have I experienced the real presence of the Risen Lord?
You are witnesses of these things (Luke 24:48). To whom is the Lord sending me this week?
pm.resp: O Lord, our God, how wonderful your name in all the earth!
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim repentance and forgiveness to every nation.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
For priests, especially those who are tired or discouraged, on this first Thursday.
For all who are frightened or doubting, that the Risen Lord may show them his wounds and give them peace.
For our group, that we may be humble witnesses who give God the glory.
pm.close: Father, you glorified your servant Jesus and raised him from the dead. Make us witnesses of his Resurrection in word and deed. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, a man who could not walk for forty years now clings to Peter and John, and a whole crowd runs together to see. Peter could have enjoyed the attention. Instead he says: why do you stare at us, as though by our own power or piety we had made him walk? (Acts 3:12). The healing belongs to Jesus.
This is a good test for all of us. When God does something good through us, do we keep the credit, or do we pass it on to him? A humble witness points away from himself, to the Risen Lord.

Then Peter says hard words: you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead. But at once he adds: I know that you acted in ignorance (Acts 3:17). He does not condemn; he invites. Repent, and turn to God so that your sins may be wiped out. Peter, who had denied the Lord, knows how good it is to be forgiven.

In the Gospel Jesus stands among his disciples and they think he is a ghost. So he says: look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself. Touch me and see (Luke 24:39). And he eats a piece of broiled fish in front of them. Our faith is not in a ghost or an idea. Jesus is truly risen in his body, the same body that was wounded for us.

Luke tells us that in their joy they were disbelieving. Sometimes the good news is so big we are afraid to believe it. Our sins forgiven? Death defeated? Heaven open? Yes. The Lord shows us his wounds so that we may dare to believe.

Then he opens the Scriptures and says: you are witnesses of these things (Luke 24:48). That word is for us too. At this Mass the Risen Lord will stand among us and give us his Body. Let us go home and be his witnesses, beginning in our own Jerusalem, our own family. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, the friends of Jesus thought they were seeing a ghost. Jesus said: touch me! And he ate a piece of fish. Jesus is really alive!
Jesus is alive with a real body, and he loves us. When you are afraid, say: Jesus, give me your peace.

intro: Theme: “You are witnesses of these things.”
Not by our own power, the Risen Lord who can be touched, and the mission of forgiveness to all nations.

sub: The man who will not let go.
Peter turns the glory to God.
Forgiven sinners call others to repent.
q: and by your offspring shall all the nations of the earth gain blessing for themselves, because you have obeyed my voice.
Repent therefore, and turn to God so that your sins may be wiped out,
points.apply: Each time you are praised today, say inwardly: “Glory to you, Lord Jesus,” and mean it.

q: what are human beings that you are mindful of them, mortals that you care for them?
Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself. Touch me and see; for a ghost does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.
points.apply: Before Communion this week, look at the crucifix and say: “It is you, Lord, truly risen, truly here.”

sub: Repentance and forgiveness for every nation.
Beginning from Jerusalem, beginning from home.
q: The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
You are witnesses of these things.
points.apply: Share with one person this week, simply and gladly, why you believe that Jesus is risen.

concl: The power that heals belongs to the Risen Lord, who forgives even those who rejected him.
He is truly risen in his body, and he sends us as witnesses of repentance and forgiveness.
2027-04-01.resolve: Say each morning of this Octave: “Lord, make me a witness of your Resurrection today.”
